transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-01 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Ramos (Redwood SE), Laura Mills (Crestpoint CTO), Evan Brooks (Head of InfoSec), Sanjay Patel (Cloud Architect), Ruth Kim (Compliance)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on data residency and compliance needs; customer leaning toward private or dedicated for regulated workloads; need to validate encryption/KMS and logging redaction.

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. miguel and i are from Redwood, i'm ava chen, account exec, and miguel's the SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Laura Mills: Good, thanks. we wanted this call to scope out what options we have for keeping data in region and aligning with our bank's compliance.
[00:15] Miguel Ramos: great, thanks laura. quick agenda: understand your regulated datasets, residency needs, retention/logging constraints, and then we can map hosted vs dedicated vs private to those requirements. sound good?
[00:24] Evan Brooks: yeah that's the core. we have two product lines: retail banking (mostly US data) and wealth management which has EU customers. some of the analytics/ML work touches SSNs, account numbers, and in a few cases medical-benefit notes from a joint product with a health partner so we need HIPAA-adjacent controls in one workflow.
[00:42] Ruth Kim: to be clear, we can't have certain tokens or raw transcripts leave EU borders for EU customers. also audit logs must be immutable and retention windows vary by dataset.
[00:52] Miguel Ramos: got it. for EU residency we can provide region pinning in hosted for some models but for guaranteed physical control we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated deployed into a specific region with contractual data residency.
[01:05] Sanjay Patel: what's the difference operationally between Dedicated and Private? i know dedicated is reserved capacity, but do we manage keys or is that redwood?
[01:12] Miguel Ramos: good question. dedicated is a Redwood-managed environment with dedicated GPU pools for your tenancy; keys are managed via Redwood KMS integrations but we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or customer HSM in many cases. private (VPC or on-prem) gives you the most control - private control plane and optionally customer-managed network and KMS.
[01:27] Evan Brooks: we need HSM-backed key control for the wealth product. can you integrate with our HSM/HSM-as-a-service?
[01:33] Miguel Ramos: yes, we have both KMS and HSM integrations; with private deployment we can do direct HSM integration, customer KMS, or bring-your-own-HSM. we'll share the integration docs.
[01:40] Laura Mills: logs are a big one. currently our security policy says raw transcripts that contain PII can't be stored longer than 30 days and must be redacted at ingestion. can your platform redact or tokenize before storage?
[01:51] Miguel Ramos: we support configurable redaction and tokenization in the ingestion path; you can apply PII detectors and mask or drop fields. for hosted, we can do redaction before logs leave the serving runtime, but you should be explicit about what you consider PII so we can show the rules.
[02:05] Ruth Kim: we also need the audit logs to be immutable and provide a tamper-evident chain for compliance audits. is that possible?
[02:12] Ava Chen: yes, we provide audit logging with write-once storage options and can integrate log shipping to your SIEM. we also have an audit export that is signed for tamper evidence. i'll send an example redacted audit export.
[02:24] Evan Brooks: any concerns about sending tokens to a hosted environment - we have a strict policy that some tokens cannot be sent to third-party managed clouds unless contractually isolated.
[02:34] Miguel Ramos: understood. that's where Dedicated or Private are better. with Dedicated we can contractually guarantee isolation and we support dedicated tenancy and pathing that limits cross-tenant host-level data exposure. with Private, you own the network and control egress completely.
[02:46] Sanjay Patel: performance-wise, if we move to private, do we lose some of the batching/cost optimizations? latency implications?
[02:53] Miguel Ramos: good point. our serving runtime is consistent across deployment modes; however, in private you might need to provision capacity to hit throughput targets. Redwood Dedicated includes autoscaling policies for predictable throughput; Private can be tuned similarly but is up to your infra team for provisioning. we can share our recommended capacity math and kernel selection notes.
[03:08] Laura Mills: okay, can you do SOC2 and HIPAA attestation for hosted?
[03:12] Ava Chen: we are SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified for our hosted service and have HIPAA BAAs available - we can share the docs. but for some of the EU residency items and HSM requirements, dedicated or private may be more appropriate.
[03:25] Ruth Kim: HIPAA BAA is important for the health-adjacent workflows. we need to review the BAAs and encryption-at-rest proofs.
[03:32] Miguel Ramos: we'll include encryption certs, KMS integration flow, and examples of configuration. also note that for HIPAA you may want to avoid third-party analytics on PHI; we can ensure model telemetry is filtered.
[03:44] Evan Brooks: telemetry and debug logs - we must ensure no raw PII in debug traces. can debug logs be disabled or filtered per environment?
[03:52] Miguel Ramos: yes, debug/tracing can be disabled or scrubbed. for Dedicated/Private we can apply stricter policies and ship only metadata, with redaction hooks.
[04:02] Laura Mills: about GDPR, we need the ability to do subject access requests (SAR) and data deletion. who handles deletion at the model cache level?
[04:10] Miguel Ramos: we provide APIs to delete user data and to purge KV cache entries. for hosted we maintain processes for SARs; for private you control deletion end-to-end. we'll send docs on data lifecycle management.
[04:22] Ava Chen: to help scope a pilot, we typically do a 4-week bench and pilot: week 1 scoping and data mapping, week 2 test harness and benchmarks, week 3 pilot with non-prod traffic, week 4 limited-prod test and evaluation. is that timeline reasonable?
[04:34] Laura Mills: yes, that could work. budget will determine whether we do dedicated or private for the pilot.
[04:39] Sanjay Patel: licensing and cost model - do you have a flat monthly for Dedicated vs per-token for hosted?
[04:45] Ava Chen: hosted is usage-based per token/embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits, and Private is enterprise licensing plus infra. i'll send a comparison sheet.
[04:54] Evan Brooks: on legal, we need to know if we can require logging restrictions in contract - e.g., prohibit storage of transcripts and require immediate redaction. is that contractable?
[05:03] Ava Chen: yes, contract clauses for data handling, deletion, and residency can be included. for high-assurance requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private with specific SLRs.
[05:12] Miguel Ramos: a couple technical clarifications - when you say "redact at ingestion," do you control the client side or do you want Redwood to run the PII detectors before we store any artifacts?
[05:21] Ruth Kim: ideally redaction should occur before anything touches long-term storage, and we might do client-side pre-filtering for extra assurance.
[05:27] Miguel Ramos: that's doable. we can support client-side redaction and server-side PII detectors as a belt-and-suspenders approach.
[05:34] Laura Mills: for EU data residency we also need data subject residency logs for audits. can you provide per-request location metadata?
[05:41] Miguel Ramos: yes, request-level metadata with region tags and signed audit logs is standard. we'll include an example audit line.
[05:48] Evan Brooks: any public benchmarks on latency for dedicated vs hosted?
[05:52] Miguel Ramos: we publish performance profiles; dedicated often yields lower and more predictable p95 latencies because of reserved GPU pools. hosting uses multi-tenant optimizations but still performs well. i'll drop links to our performance profiles and a short benchmark plan.
[06:03] Ava Chen: just to surface common objections - some banks are worried about vendor lock-in. we support export mechanisms for model config and cache dumps and allow pinning to open models so you can migrate.
[06:15] Laura Mills: ok that's helpful.

[06:20] Recap:
- Customer requires EU and US residency guarantees for certain datasets and HSM-backed keys for one product line.
- Logging: redaction at ingestion, immutable audit logs, retention variable by dataset (some <30 days).
- Preferred next step: send compliance artifacts and schedule a technical deep dive / bench test planning.

[06:40] Closing notes:
Ava Chen: thanks everyone we'll get docs over by Wednesday and Miguel will follow up with network diagrams. we'll propose times for the deep dive.
[06:48] Laura Mills: thanks, looking forward to the docs.

(Transcript ends - automated timestamps approximate, speaker attribution auto-generated, occasional transcription errors present.)
